records.title: Introduction to Urbanization: Planning and Designing Alternative Urban Futures
records.header: URBAN 200 Introduction to Urbanization: Planning and Designing Alternative Urban Futures (5) SSc
records.text: URBAN 200 Introduction to Urbanization: Planning and Designing Alternative Urban Futures (5) SSc Introduces how cities work and explores alternative ways of planning and designing urban futures. Explores the economic, cultural, political, and social aspects of cities and how we might change them for the better. Also examines numerous case studies from the Global North and South.

records.title: Survey of Urban Planning and the Built Environment
records.header: URBAN 250 Survey of Urban Planning and the Built Environment (5) SSc
records.text: URBAN 250 Survey of Urban Planning and the Built Environment (5) SSc Introduces students to the field of urban design and planning. Explores key theories, practices, and specializations, from transportation to urban design. Examines real-world challenges in the Puget Sound region. Guest speakers and case studies connect classroom learning to professional practice in shaping sustainable, livable communities. Offered: W.

records.title: Introduction to Urban Planning
records.header: URBAN 300 Introduction to Urban Planning (5) SSc
records.text: URBAN 300 Introduction to Urban Planning (5) SSc Principles and theories of urban structure and institutions. Concepts and logic of planning as a community process and a professional activity. Evolution of planning ideas in response to changing social, economic, and environmental conditions within the American political framework. Complementary nature of public and private responsibilities. Major procedures used by planners.

records.title: Reading the City
records.text: URBAN 370 Reading the City (5) A&H/SSc Comprehending cities as reflection of individual reader and social/cultural context. Skills for analyzing everyday, visible evidence of the city. Topics include self-identity with place, city, image and perception, visual design analysis; and place as representation of culture. Extensive writing, multiple texts, collaborative work in groups and fieldwork.

records.title: Urban and Regional Geospatial Analysis
records.header: URBAN 422 Urban and Regional Geospatial Analysis (5)
records.text: URBAN 422 Urban and Regional Geospatial Analysis (5) Principles of GIS applied to problems in urban design and planning, landscape architecture, and environmental and resource studies. Practical problem-solving approaches using contemporary desktop mapping packages and vector and raster GIS systems. Siting, environmental evaluation and inventories, and modeling. Prerequisite: either GEOG 317, GEOG 360, GEOG 461, GEOG 462, GEOG 465, or OCEAN 452/FISH 452. Offered: W.

records.text: URBAN 424 Site Planning: Issues and Techniques (3) Introduction to site planning; how it is regulated; why it is important to know; and how to carry out its key tasks, including residential subdivision and mixed-use development layout; basic topographical and hydrological analysis and manipulation; roadways, parking and hierarchies of circulation, and site design detail. records.title: Healthy Urbanism
records.text: URBAN 435 Healthy Urbanism (5) SSc Explores how urban environments and policies impact health and wellbeing. Introduces healthy urbanism and socio-ecological models, showing how sectors beyond healthcare shape outcomes. Students gain skills to promote health across disciplines, focusing on equity, sustainability, and real-world policy solutions. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Infrastructure and Community Facilities
records.text: URBAN 466 Infrastructure and Community Facilities (4) Issues and methods associated with planning for parks, schools, drainage, sewerage, utilities, libraries, solid waste, and transportation. Covers their relationship to comprehensive plans, project permitting, and impact assessment. Financing, regulating, and relationships to social, environmental, and economic goals are discussed.

records.title: Planning as a Profession
records.header: URBAN 480 Planning as a Profession (1, max. 3)
records.text: URBAN 480 Planning as a Profession (1, max. 3) Provides students interested in the planning profession an opportunity to understand the different pathways and career choices within the profession. Introduces students to guest professionals in various planning careers and highlights key issues, skills used, and tips to entering the field. Focuses on professional practice rather than analytical methods or theory. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.
